messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: umbra-enterprise VPC showing sustained 502/504s from ap-southeast-1 dedicated pool (umbra-dedicated-ap1). Alert: 502 rate > 6% for 4m.
Alex (oncall): Ack. Picking this up.
Alex (oncall): Priya, handing off — any recent changes?
Priya (prev-oncall): Handoff: I rotated certs on pool nodes at 02:10 but validated. No immediate errors then. I did see conntrack spikes later.
Alex (oncall): Copy. Checking canaries & infra.
Sofia (platform): Synthetic canaries started failing at 09:04:15 UTC. Logs show upstream reset "RST" from app runtime on 3 hosts.
Haruto (networking): Also seeing increased TCP RSTs at the LB layer. Could be NAT gateway conntrack exhaustion in ap-southeast-1 for this tenant's VPC.
Dean (support): Customer (Umbra) on call; they report intermittent 502s and sticky sessions breaking. They say some requests succeed but many time out at 30s.
Alex (oncall): Good to know. If conntrack is the cause we might need to divert traffic to warm standby in ap-northeast-1 until we scale NAT. Do we have warm capacity?
Priya (prev-oncall): Yes, there is umbra-warm-ap2 at 25% warm.
Sofia (platform): Confirmed. Warm pool image aligned. However, session affinity requires IP-level persistence; we need to preserve session cookies. Route-shift will preserve sticky cookie header via our gateway.
Alex (oncall): Plan: 1) Start short canary 15% to ap-northeast-1 warm pool. 2) Scale NATs in ap-southeast-1 and increase conntrack max. 3) If canary stable at 5m, move remainder and drain failing nodes. 4) Inform customer of cutover and IP-affinity implications.
ops-bot: Runbook: TENANT_FAILOVER: umbra-enterprise -> warm ap-northeast-1. Steps initiated by Alex.
Alex (oncall): Executing canary now: `console route shift --tenant umbra-enterprise --to-region ap-northeast-1 --percent 15`
incidents-bot: Route shift job created (job_id: rs-2145697777-A). Monitoring.
Haruto (networking): Lowering DNS TTL for umbra.api.redwood.com to 20s for cutover. Also prepping BGP anycast withdrawal if needed.
Sofia (platform): Canary metrics: canary nodes show success rate improved from 91% -> 99.4%, p95 latency reduced ~60ms.
Dean (support): Customer on call confirms success on canary endpoints. They report fewer timeouts.
Alex (oncall): Scaling NAT gateway count and bumping conntrack: `aws cli conntrack set --vpc-id vpc-umbra --max 200k` (internal command).
Priya (prev-oncall): Note: conntrack tweak requires node pool restart for some managed NATs. That will be staged.
Haruto (networking): While NAT scales, do we want to shift more traffic? My suggestion: go to 60% to relieve pressure but keep 40% to allow session finish.
Alex (oncall): Agreed. Moving to 60% now. `console route shift --tenant umbra-enterprise --percent 60`
incidents-bot: Route shift job updated (job_id: rs-2145697777-B). Percent moved: 60%.
Sofia (platform): After shift to 60%, error rate for tenant dropped to 0.7%. Some regional LBs still showing elevated connections; draining nodes flagged with high conntrack usage.
Priya (prev-oncall): Starting maintenance drain on 4 hosts in ap-southeast-1: mark nodes standby, start graceful connection drain 300s.
Dean (support): Customer grateful. They requested that we keep them in the loop and asked about any backend data loss.
Alex (oncall): Confirmed: no request-level data loss observed; most failures are connection-level timeouts. Logging shows retries succeeding once routed to ap-northeast-1.
Haruto (networking): We observed a spike in ephemeral port exhaustion on NATs coincident with an increase in client-side retry storms from one of Umbra's legacy SDKs. We flagged mitigation with rate-limiting at the edge.
Sofia (platform): Applying short-term ingress token bucket: `edge rate-limit apply --tenant umbra-enterprise --rate 120rps` to prevent retry storms.
incidents-bot: Rate limit applied.
Dean (support): Customer confirms their dev team will push a patch to reduce client-side aggressive retries. They appreciate the edge throttle.
Alex (oncall): After 20m stable, proceed to 100% cutover if no regressions. Current timeline fine.
Sofia (platform): Preparing final cutover. Also snapshotting current routing configs and session-cookie mapping.
Alex (oncall): Executing final shift to 100% now. `console route shift --tenant umbra-enterprise --percent 100`
incidents-bot: Final route shift job completed (job_id: rs-2145697777-C). Traffic fully served from ap-northeast-1 warm pool. :white_check_mark:
Haruto (networking): Rolling BGP anycast route adjustments are not required now. We kept DNS-based cutover.
Sofia (platform): Initiating scaled-down NAT in ap-southeast-1 once drained hosts are healthy; will apply permanent conntrack tuning as per runbook. Ticket filed: PROD-4291.
Priya (prev-oncall): I'll coordinate with runtime to harden conntrack defaults and add canary for conntrack pressure on future deploys.
Dean (support): Communicated full cutover and suggested next steps to Umbra: permanent fix timeline, client SDK patch, and postmortem. They want an ETA for controller fix.
Alex (oncall): Postmortem owner: Alex. Action items: 1) Runtime default conntrack increase + tests, 2) Edge retry throttling per-tenant, 3) Improve canary to detect conntrack-like symptoms, 4) Customer SDK guidance doc.
incidents-bot: Severity downgraded to Sev3. Incident page: https://incidents.redwood.internal/2145697777
Alex (oncall): Postmortem link created: https://docs.redwood.internal/postmortems/2145697777-umbra-conntrack-failover
Dean (support): Sending customer summary and postmortem link.
Haruto (networking): Will follow up with network runbook updates and add BGP escalation checklist.
Alex (oncall): Closing thread. Thanks all. :checkered_flag:
